VibePascal v61 Linux x86_64 compiler -- a with-statement interface prefix lives exactly as long as its statement: never freed under the body, never leaked to routine exit

Contents: bin/ppcx64 and bin/ppudump -- a COMPILER-BINARY refresh meant to drop into an existing VibePascal
source/unit tree on Linux.  The v59 x86_64-linux unit set (dist/linux64/vibepascal-v59-x86_64-linux-units.tar.gz, see
UNITS.txt) stays valid and does not need rebuilding: no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE v59 -- TWO DEFECTS, ONE CAUSE, BOTH ONLY WHEN THE WITH WAS NOT THE FIRST STATEMENT OF ITS BLOCK
  tblocknode.simplify splices a compiler-built statement list (the hidden pieces of a with statement: prefix temp
  create, its assignment, the body, the temp deletes) into the enclosing begin..end when the with is not the first
  statement there.  Since v59 numbers and releases interface temps per source statement, every spliced piece became
  a statement of its own:
    * "with Make.o do begin ... end" (Make returns a COM interface, .o is the raw object): the assignment piece
      released the interface BEFORE the body ran, so the body worked on a freed object.  Present in v59 AND v60.
    * "with Make do begin ... end": the prefix temps were deleted under marks newer than their own stamp and
      leaked until routine exit (v59).  GOD's 407ef9bb3a (v60) closed this half and stays in.
  v61 never merges a compiler-built list into a source block (a nested begin..end still may be: its statements are
  real ones).  Nothing is released earlier than the end of the with statement, and nothing later.

HOW THIS BINARY WAS PROVEN (all on THESE bytes)
  * tests/test/tintfwithprefix1.pp (new, 62 corners): checks=62 fails=0 created=56 destroyed=56 live=0 at -O- and -O2;
    the published v59 prints 16 FAIL lines on it, the v60 linux build 5 (the raw pointer corners).
  * tests/test/tintfstmttemp1.pp 32/32, tintfstmttemp2.pp 28/28 created=27 destroyed=27 live=0, tintflifetime1.pp 28/28.
  * 1987-test corpus A/B against the v60 linux build, and against the PUBLISHED v59: see dist/RELEASE-v61.txt for the
    numbers (the one intended DIFF is tintfwithprefix1 itself, which fails on the older compiler by design).
  * self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux: stage 2 == stage 3 byte-identical.
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh and dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh x86_64-linux: numbers in dist/RELEASE-v61.txt.
